comment: How the page presents each release of the firmware: the name it goes by here, and a line about where it stands. A release that is not listed is shown by its own state on GitHub (verified, untested or draft). `pending` names what the page will list once its files are in a release.

release-2026-11-15.label: Bastet 0.9, portrait screen
release-2026-11-15.note: Use only if Anubis gives trouble. Master 0.11.0 and Remote ID sensor 0.7.3.

notes: The unit doesn't detect DJI's DroneID signal, and a DJI OcuSync link on 2.4 GHz can show as a remote control.

release-2026-11-16-beta.label: Anubis 1.0, landscape screen
release-2026-11-16-beta.note: Use this release. One complete set, tested on two units through the night of 15 to 16 Nov 2026: master 0.12.0, Remote ID sensor 0.7.3, and the RF sensor for the Seeed XIAO ESP32-C5 or the Waveshare ESP32-C5-Zero.

rf-a2a45f2-ipex-zero.hardware: Waveshare ESP32-C5-Zero, antenna on its IPEX socket
notes: A measuring build for troubleshooting a demo, from a change that isn't merged yet. Its source code will be published later.

A "control 2.4 GHz" alert can come from a Wi-Fi or DJI aircraft, not only from a remote control. In bench tests a simulated Wi-Fi drone link showed as control in 1 of 3 runs, and an imitation of DJI's OcuSync link in 3 of 3.
Digital video on 5.8 GHz is reported only when the signal is strong. At bench distance HDZero was listed, but Walksnail and DJI OcuSync on 5.8 GHz were missed.
In a 2.4-hour test with none of our transmitters on, this build reported no remote control links.
rf-a2a45f2-ipex-zero.label: Waveshare ESP32-C5-Zero

rf-6da55bc-xiao.label: Seeed XIAO ESP32-C5
notes: A measuring build for troubleshooting a demo, from a change that isn't merged yet. Its source code will be published later.

A "control 2.4 GHz" alert can come from a Wi-Fi or DJI aircraft, not only from a remote control. In bench tests a simulated Wi-Fi drone link showed as control in 1 of 3 runs, and an imitation of DJI's OcuSync link in 3 of 3.
Digital video on 5.8 GHz is reported only when the signal is strong. At bench distance HDZero was listed, but Walksnail and DJI OcuSync on 5.8 GHz were missed.
In a 7.4-hour test with none of our transmitters on, this build reported a remote control link 22 times, about 3 an hour. The longest lasted 48 seconds. The cause isn't known.
A Wi-Fi aircraft's row can show the name of a nearby Wi-Fi network instead of the aircraft's own. The alert itself is correct.
The unit doesn't detect DJI's DroneID signal, and a DJI OcuSync link on 2.4 GHz can show as a remote control.
